ashley_devex: FYI running into a reproducible DX bug: AsyncClient drops our request_id context when retries/backoff or the SDKbatcher spawn background tasks. Minimal repro below.

ashley_devex: ```py
# repro: asyncio + redwood async client + contextvar
import asyncio
from contextvars import ContextVar
from redwood import AsyncClient
req = ContextVar('request_id')
async def main():
    req.set('rid-999')
    c = AsyncClient(retry_policy={'max_attempts':2}, instrumentor_enabled=True)
    await c.generate_async('ping')  # logs in retry attempt missing request_id
asyncio.run(main())
```

ryan_sdk: Thanks, that looks like contextvars not being carried into child tasks we spawn for backoff/flush. We switched a path to anyio/TaskGroup recently which changes scheduling semantics.

kevin_infra: Can you confirm whether this only fails with the otel instrumentor or also with plain structlog-bound context? We need to know if baggage propagation is involved.

ashley_devex: Repro is much more consistent with the otel instrumentor on; sometimes structlog-binding survives but not reliable. When otel is enabled, span exporters run in background tasks and we lose the contextvar in those code paths.

mira_obs: I'm thinking API-wise: we should provide a small, typed observability callback surface on the client so integrators can rebind context explicitly where needed. Also add convenience adapters for structlog and otel. Example:

```
client = AsyncClient()
client.register_observer('emit_log', my_fn)
client.bind_contextvar('request_id', my_contextvar)
client.instrument_opentelemetry()
```

ryan_sdk: I prefer a Protocol-based type for ergonomics. Proposal:

```
class ObsHook(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, event: str, attrs: Mapping[str,str]) -> Optional[Awaitable[None]]: ...
```
Client.register_observer(name: str, hook: ObsHook) accepts either sync or async callables; the client will detect awaitable return values and await them. That keeps parity for sync/async environments.

kevin_infra: Long-term fix is to centralise task spawn so we always preserve contextvars. e.g. provide a single helper: _spawn_task(coro) that does ctx = contextvars.copy_context(); ctx.run(asyncio.create_task, coro). We'll need to audit all places we spawn tasks (retry backoff, batcher, token refresh, exporter).

mira_obs: Agreed. Also add a small integration test in devex/sample-apps/tests that: 1) sets a ContextVar, 2) triggers a transient error to force a retry/backoff, 3) asserts emitted logs and OpenTelemetry span/baggage contain request_id. That should be part of CI for SDK changes.

ashley_devex: For a short-term workaround I wrote a tiny wrapper to snapshot the contextvar and rebind inside hook calls:

```py
def snapshot_and_call(hook):
    async def wrapped(*a, **kw):
        token = req.set(req.get(None))
        try:
            r = hook(*a, **kw)
            if asyncio.iscoroutine(r):
                await r
        finally:
            req.reset(token)
    return wrapped
```
Not ideal but proves the API shape.

ryan_sdk: Action plan I will put in a draft PR: 1) add ObsHook Protocol + register_observer API (typed), 2) central _spawn_task helper that preserves contextvars and replace a few hotspots (retry, batcher) in one change, 3) small convenience adapters: bind_contextvar and instrument_opentelemetry, 4) add integration test in devex/sample-apps/tests/test_context_propagation.py, 5) add doc note about performance considerations for synchronous vs async hooks and cautions about awaiting hooks on hot paths.

kevin_infra: Minimal patch that only changes internal task spawning is fine for quick merge. Hook API can be follow-up to avoid large surface changes. Please include microbenchmarks for hook overhead in the PR.

ci-bot: created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/621 11 CI queued.

mira_obs: In the PR description include an explicit acceptance test: the integration test must fail on current main and pass after the fix. Also include a short sample-app demonstrating both structlog binding and otel baggage mapping.

ashley_devex: Will paste failing logs into the PR and include the tiny repro harness. Thanks all.

ryan_sdk: I'll tag @mira_obs in the PR so the test expectations for OTEL are clear. Planning to ship the spawn helper in this patch and follow up with the typed hook surface and adapters.

kevin_infra: Sounds good. Once the spawn helper lands we'll follow up with an audit for other spawn sites and a rollout plan (canary in dedicated).

mira_obs: One more note: make sure instrument_opentelemetry() documents that SDK may prefer copying otel baggage into contextvars for consistency since some instrumentors rely on contextvar-only propagation. That avoids surprises.

ashley_devex: Great. I'm adding a short onboarding doc blurb: "If you rely on application ContextVars for correlation, prefer binding them via client.bind_contextvar until propagation is stabilised."
